cells.tense: You are keeping something alive right now, on purpose.
cells.verb: tending a fire that others draw warmth from
cells.place: in the becoming of who you have always been
cells.ask: offer one piece of what you carry to someone who would take it — and let what you get back feed the next step rather than only the next load
cells.core: You are tending something that keeps other people moving — not with force, with warmth, with showing up again tomorrow. It has not burned you out, because you are feeding it and not just guarding it. There is a steadiness in you that people lean on without knowing they are doing it, and it is not a performance. It is what you are like when you are most yourself.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it burning without burning yourself up.

cells.tense: You are already holding up a tomorrow that no one has handed you yet.
cells.verb: keeping a fire roaring for a room that is still empty
cells.place: in a becoming that keeps getting pushed ahead of itself
cells.ask: let one thing you are already carrying be checked, not just pushed — what comes back will tell you what is actually yours to hold, and quiet will return to the room
cells.core: You are motivating, pushing, holding the pace for something that has not arrived — and you have already decided what it needs to hear before it has asked. The care is real. The timing is off, and the strain is showing in how much you keep doing alone. You are not short on drive. You are short on letting anyone else tell you where it is going.
cells.sheetLine: You are carrying the fire for a room that is still empty.

lint.detail: the tense sentence does not read as Too Much's time

cells.tense: The fire you once kept is behind you, and you are still standing where it went out.
cells.verb: letting a fire that was yours go cold
cells.place: at the edge of a becoming you stopped walking toward
cells.ask: let one thing end that has already ended — release what is finished, simply, and take the first small step toward what actually wants to grow in its place
cells.core: You know how to keep something going — you did it, and then somewhere back there you stopped. It was not laziness. Holding it began to cost something you could not name, so you set it down and called it practicality. What is missing now is not motivation. It is permission to let one chapter close so the next one can start.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped tending it, and you have not let anything take its place.

cells.tense: The work is already happening — you are just not signing it.
cells.verb: keeping the fire warm and calling it the weather
cells.place: in a becoming you are already living but not naming
cells.ask: say it is yours, once, to one person — and let what needs to shift start shifting
cells.core: You are already doing the thing — holding the direction, keeping people going, being the reason something is still alive. You talk about it as if it happens around you. The doing is real. What you have not said is that it is you doing it, and that gap is the whole difference between a job and a life.
cells.sheetLine: You are already holding it. You keep calling it someone else's job.
